lec05kp10-scene-u01.name: Network size, generalization and early stopping

lec05kp10-u01-p1-title.text: Same noisy samples: the smooth trend is learning, a polyline through every point memorizes noise

lec05kp10-u01-p1-bridge.name: u01-p1-bridge
lec05kp10-u01-p1-bridge.text: Does a high training score mean new data is predicted well? What must controlling network size avoid?

lec05kp10-u01-p1-nf-lec05-kp10-p1-1.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p1|10 noisy samples, the smooth curve sin(2πx) and a polyline through every point; the polyline is only an illustration.

lec05kp10-u01-p1-nf-lec05-kp10-p1-4.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p1#4
lec05kp10-u01-p1-nf-lec05-kp10-p1-4.text: The same noisy samples: a smooth trend versus a memorizing polyline (illustrative)

lec05kp10-u01-p1-nf-lec05-kp10-p1-108.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p1#108
lec05kp10-u01-p1-nf-lec05-kp10-p1-108.text: Yellow: 10 noisy samples; the polyline memorized the noise too. (illustration only)

lec05kp10-u01-p1-nf-lec05-kp10-p1-111.name: term:Generalization

lec05kp10-u01-p1-nf-lec05-kp10-p1-113.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p1#113
lec05kp10-u01-p1-nf-lec05-kp10-p1-113.text:
Controlling size means avoiding
memorizing the training data.

lec05kp10-u01-p1-nf-lec05-kp10-p1-114.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p1#114
lec05kp10-u01-p1-nf-lec05-kp10-p1-114.text:
Classification has the same trade-off:
find the main pattern first; not every
wiggle is a rule.

lec05kp10-u01-p1-nf-lec05-kp10-p1-116.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p1#116
lec05kp10-u01-p1-nf-lec05-kp10-p1-116.text: A high training score does not mean new data is predicted well: tell memorizing from learning first.

lec05kp10-u01-p2-title.name: u01-p2-title
lec05kp10-u01-p2-title.text: A 2–3–1 network has 13 free parameters: hidden (2+1)×3 = 9, output (3+1)×1 = 4, not just 3 units

lec05kp10-u01-p2-bridge.name: u01-p2-bridge
lec05kp10-u01-p2-bridge.text: The polyline memorized the noise while the smooth trend is learning. How many adjustable numbers does a network actually have?

lec05kp10-u01-p2-nf-lec05-kp10-p2-1.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p2|A 2–3–1 network diagram with the parameter count: 9 in the hidden layer, 4 in the output layer, 13 free parameters.

lec05kp10-u01-p2-nf-lec05-kp10-p2-4.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p2#4
lec05kp10-u01-p2-nf-lec05-kp10-p2-4.text: A 2–3–1 network: fully connected, every unit has a bias

lec05kp10-u01-p2-nf-lec05-kp10-p2-39.name: term:Free parameter

lec05kp10-u01-p2-nf-lec05-kp10-p2-40.name: term:Underfitting
lec05kp10-u01-p2-nf-lec05-kp10-p2-40.text:
Underfitting: the model cannot even
express the main pattern, so
performance can be poor on both
training and new data.

lec05kp10-u01-p2-nf-lec05-kp10-p2-41.name: term:Overfitting
lec05kp10-u01-p2-nf-lec05-kp10-p2-41.text:
Overfitting: fitting chance details of
the training data, which hurts
predictions on new data.

lec05kp10-u01-p2-nf-lec05-kp10-p2-43.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p2#43
lec05kp10-u01-p2-nf-lec05-kp10-p2-43.text: "Larger" is not sufficient for overfitting: data size, weight size, constraints and training all matter.

lec05kp10-u01-p3-title.name: u01-p3-title
lec05kp10-u01-p3-title.text: Validation loss bottoms at 0.25 in epoch 3, then rises to 0.40: keep epoch 3 (early stopping)

lec05kp10-u01-p3-bridge.name: u01-p3-bridge
lec05kp10-u01-p3-bridge.text: A 2–3–1 network has 13 free parameters and the architecture is fixed. How long should we train?

lec05kp10-u01-p3-nf-lec05-kp10-p3-1.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p3|Training and validation loss at five checkpoints; validation is lowest at 0.25 in epoch 3 and rises to 0.40 in epoch 5, while training is lowest at 0.10 in epoch 5.

lec05kp10-u01-p3-nf-lec05-kp10-p3-4.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p3#4
lec05kp10-u01-p3-nf-lec05-kp10-p3-4.text: Training and validation loss at each checkpoint (hand-made teaching numbers)

lec05kp10-u01-p3-nf-lec05-kp10-p3-56.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p3#56
lec05kp10-u01-p3-nf-lec05-kp10-p3-56.text:
The dashed line marks epoch 3, the one to keep; the curves need not cross and the
gap need not start at zero.

lec05kp10-u01-p3-nf-lec05-kp10-p3-59.name: term:Validation set
lec05kp10-u01-p3-nf-lec05-kp10-p3-59.text:
Validation set: data not used to update weights,
used to pick a model or a checkpoint.

lec05kp10-u01-p3-nf-lec05-kp10-p3-60.name: term:Overtraining
lec05kp10-u01-p3-nf-lec05-kp10-p3-60.text:
Overtraining: with a fixed architecture, later
training chases training-set details and validation
performance worsens.

lec05kp10-u01-p3-nf-lec05-kp10-p3-61.name: term:Early stopping
lec05kp10-u01-p3-nf-lec05-kp10-p3-61.text:
Early stopping: stop training by validation
performance and restore the best checkpoint;
implementations may allow a few non-improving
checks.

lec05kp10-u01-p3-nf-lec05-kp10-p3-64.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p3#64
lec05kp10-u01-p3-nf-lec05-kp10-p3-64.text: Epoch 5 has the lowest training loss (0.10) but validation rose from 0.25 to 0.40, an increase of 0.40 − 0.25 = 0.15.

lec05kp10-u01-p4-title.name: u01-p4-title
lec05kp10-u01-p4-title.text: Training, validation, test: three data sets, three jobs; the test set only comes after model choice

lec05kp10-u01-p4-bridge.name: u01-p4-bridge
lec05kp10-u01-p4-bridge.text: Validation loss bottoms at 0.25 in epoch 3, then rises to 0.40, so we keep epoch 3. With validation data used to choose, which data reports the final score?

lec05kp10-u01-p4-nf-lec05-kp10-p4-1.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p4|The use and limits of the training, validation and test sets, and the small-sample error rates 0.1 for one error and 0.2 for two.

lec05kp10-u01-p4-nf-lec05-kp10-p4-6.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p4#6
lec05kp10-u01-p4-nf-lec05-kp10-p4-6.text:
Used to update the weights and learn
the pattern.

lec05kp10-u01-p4-nf-lec05-kp10-p4-8.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p4#8
lec05kp10-u01-p4-nf-lec05-kp10-p4-8.text:
Cannot judge accuracy on new data: it
has been seen already.

lec05kp10-u01-p4-nf-lec05-kp10-p4-12.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p4#12
lec05kp10-u01-p4-nf-lec05-kp10-p4-12.text:
Used to choose the size, the penalty
strength and the stopping point.

lec05kp10-u01-p4-nf-lec05-kp10-p4-18.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p4#18
lec05kp10-u01-p4-nf-lec05-kp10-p4-18.text:
Used for the final evaluation only after
the model is chosen.

lec05kp10-u01-p4-nf-lec05-kp10-p4-20.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p4#20
lec05kp10-u01-p4-nf-lec05-kp10-p4-20.text:
Reusing it to pick models ends its
independence; also avoid duplicate or
time-information leakage.

lec05kp10-u01-p4-nf-lec05-kp10-p4-25.name: fig:lec05-kp10-p4#25

lec05kp10-u01-p4-nf-lec05-kp10-p4-29.text:
One more case moves the estimate ten points.
Repeated splits or cross-validation help; keep
training and evaluation apart.

lec05kp10-u01-p4-nf-lec05-kp10-p4-31.text: Myth: fewer parameters or longer training do not each guarantee better accuracy; no universal best neuron count.

Start from a small architecture and

steps.label: Network size, generalization and early stopping
steps.speakerNotes: Level: undergraduate (year 3). Made from the lecture lec05-kp10 with view-from-text-v3: pages were planned first and each page is mainly one native infographic (designed in HTML and converted to native nodes), with the terms defined on the same page. 10 pages; every number is computed by program. The polyline on page 1 and the five checkpoint numbers on page 3 are teaching illustrations and hand-made numbers, not network training results; the sine-demo setup on page 8 is the source's report and was not rerun.

steps.label: Memorizing vs learning
steps.speakerNotes: This is the first page of KP10. The prerequisites are loss and cost (KP06, KP09), forward pass and parameters (KP06) and hyperplanes (KP03). This page first separates memorizing from learning. Generalization means still predicting new data that was not used in training, not memorizing the original answers. The yellow dots are 10 noisy samples, the green curve is the smooth trend sin(2πx), and the red dashed polyline passes through every point: it memorized the noise instead of learning the pattern. This is a supplementary illustration for continuous prediction and the polyline is not a trained network. Classification faces the same trade-off: find the main pattern first, then look at the small wiggles; not every wiggle is a rule. Controlling network size means avoiding memorizing the training data. Next, the next page covers counting free parameters.

steps.label: Free parameters
steps.speakerNotes: Following the previous page on memorizing versus learning. This page counts free parameters: numbers that training can change independently, weights and biases both counting. The example has two inputs, three hidden units and one output, fully connected, with a bias in every computing unit. Each hidden unit has 2 weights plus 1 bias, (2 plus 1) times 3 equal to 9; the output has 3 weights plus 1 bias, (3 plus 1) times 1 equal to 4; in total 9 plus 4 equal to 13, not just the three hidden units (computed by program). Two opposite failures: underfitting cannot even express the main pattern; overfitting fits chance details of the training data and hurts predictions on new data. Larger is not sufficient for overfitting; data size, weight size, constraints and the training procedure all matter. Next, the next page covers early stopping on validation data.

steps.label: Early stopping
steps.speakerNotes: Following the previous page on counting free parameters. A fixed size can still overfit the training data, so training time must be controlled separately. The validation set is data not used to update weights, used to pick a model or a checkpoint; overtraining is when, with a fixed architecture, later training chases training-set details and validation performance worsens; early stopping stops training by validation performance and restores the best checkpoint, and implementations may allow a few non-improving checks. These are hand-made teaching numbers, not experimental results: training loss 0.50, 0.30, 0.20, 0.15, 0.10 and validation loss 0.55, 0.35, 0.25, 0.28, 0.40. The validation minimum is 0.25 at epoch 3, so keep the weights of epoch 3; epoch 5 has the lowest training loss, yet validation rose from 0.25 to 0.40, an increase of 0.40 minus 0.25 equal to 0.15 (computed by program). The two curves need not cross and the gap need not start at zero. Next, the next page covers the roles of the three data sets.

steps.label: Three data sets
steps.speakerNotes: Following the previous page on early stopping on validation data. The three data sets have separate jobs. The training set updates the weights and learns the pattern; the validation set chooses the size, penalty strength and stopping point and does not update weights directly; the test set is used for the final evaluation only after the model is chosen, and looking at it again and again to pick models ends its independence, while duplicate individuals or time information must not leak. Small-sample numbers are coarse: one error in ten is 1 over 10 equal to 0.1; two errors give 0.2, so one more case moves the estimate by ten percentage points (computed by program). Repeated splits or cross-validation can help, but training and evaluation stay separate each time and independent data cannot be created from nothing, so no best number of neurons exists apart from data size and task. Common myth: fewer parameters or longer training do not each guarantee better new-data accuracy. Next, the next page covers the region-count bound.

steps.label: Region-count bound
steps.speakerNotes: Following the previous page on the roles of the three data sets. Data choices answer whether predictions are good, while geometric counting only answers how many regions the architecture can cut at most; they are different questions. With K hyperplanes cutting d-dimensional space, the number of regions is at most M_max(K, d), the sum over m from 0 to d of C(K, m); C(K, m) is the number of ways to choose m of K and is 0 when m exceeds K. The maximum is reached only in general position, that is, with no coincident, parallel or concurrent hyperplanes. Value table: for d equal to 1 and K from 1 to 4 it is 2, 3, 4, 5; for d equal to 2 it is 2, 4, 7, 11; for d equal to 3 it is 2, 4, 8, 15 (computed by program). Example: d equal to 2 and K equal to 2 gives 1 plus 2 plus 1 equal to 4, the three binomials being choices of 0, 1 and 2 lines. In the chart, the higher the dimension and the more hyperplanes, the faster the maximum grows. Next, the next page covers the explicit XOR construction.

steps.label: XOR construction
steps.speakerNotes: Following the previous page on the region-count bound. The explicit XOR construction: the KP01 lines x1 plus x2 equal to 0.5 and x1 plus x2 equal to 1.5 are parallel and actually cut only three bands. The sums x1 plus x2 at the four points are 0 at (0,0), 1 at (0,1) and (1,0), and 2 at (1,1) (computed by program): 0 is below 0.5, in the lower band, class B; 1 lies between 0.5 and 1.5, in the middle band where both A points live; 2 is above 1.5, in the upper band, class B. That four regions of the bound hold three is only a capacity check; whether two units suffice must be proved by this explicit construction. Next, the next page covers the three sizing strategies.

steps.label: Three strategies
steps.speakerNotes: Following the previous page on the explicit XOR construction. The bound does not tell us how to find a suitable size. In practice there are three strategies: analytic methods estimate capability with algebra or statistics but usually ignore the actual optimization process; pruning trains a larger network first and then deletes the less important connections by a rule, which the next KP covers; constructive methods start from a small architecture and add units step by step, as KP05 showed. All three routes need checking on validation data. Next, the next page covers the source's sine demo.

steps.label: Sine demo
steps.speakerNotes: Following the previous page on the three sizing strategies. The source has a sine demo; we only describe its setup and do not treat one experiment as a general optimum. The target is y equal to sin(2πx) plus ε, where ε is noise added to the observations; the data are 15 training points and 10 independent test points; the model is ŷ equal to the sum over j from 1 to k of v_j tanh(a_j x plus b_j) plus c, where k is the number of hidden units and a_j, b_j, v_j and c are all adjustable, so the parameter count is 3k plus 1: 10 for k equal to 3, 16 for k equal to 5 and 46 for k equal to 15 (computed by program). The source describes k of about 3 to 5 as suitable and k equal to 15 as possibly overfitting. This is not a universal best value for any data, and the training was not rerun here. Next, the next page covers the region recursion.

steps.label: Extension: recursion
steps.speakerNotes: Following the previous page on the source's sine demo. Why the region count has this form: adding the K-th hyperplane in general position splits some existing regions in two; the new pieces correspond to the lower-dimensional regions that the other K minus 1 hyperplanes form inside the new plane, so R(K, d) equals R(K minus 1, d) plus R(K minus 1, d minus 1), starting from R(0, d) and R(K, 0) both equal to 1; Pascal's rule gives the sum of C(K, m). R(3, 2) equals R(2, 2) plus R(2, 1) equal to 4 plus 3 equal to 7, agreeing with 1 plus 3 plus 3 (computed by program). This derivation only counts space partitions and does not include whether the output layer can label any region correctly. Top right is the mean squared error L equal to one over N times the sum of squared errors for continuous prediction; errors 1 and minus 1 give 1; classification needs a threshold and an error rate separately. The code at the bottom right only selects among given checkpoints and trains no network; real training must also save and restore that epoch's weights, fix the data split and record the metric. Next, the next page covers the exercises.

steps.label: Extension: exercises
steps.speakerNotes: Following the previous page on the region recursion. Two exercises. Q1: training loss 0.40, 0.20, 0.10 and validation loss 0.45, 0.25, 0.30; which epoch? Among the validation values 0.25 is the smallest, so keep epoch 2; the lower training value of the last epoch does not change the choice; epoch 3 validation is 0.30 minus 0.25 equal to 0.05 higher than epoch 2. Q2: the maximum number of regions of three lines in general position in 2-D is C(3,0) plus C(3,1) plus C(3,2) equal to 1 plus 3 plus 3 equal to 7; three parallel lines give only four bands, not reaching seven; check: the geometric region count plays no part in choosing a checkpoint (computed by program). That ends this unit; the next KP covers pruning, regularization and simulations.
